- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–4% to capture mean reversion.
- Model exhibits strong lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the forecast window; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid overextension.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
